# Two causal endpoints: public relay and private persistence

## S1's future-noun effect is overwhelmingly public

At \(5\times\), S1 changes the free article from `a` to `an` on 19/20 held-out
prompts and changes the top noun on the same 19. Across all 20 prompts, total
noun-distribution change is 0.893 TV. Replaying the treated article with the
intervention off produces 0.891 TV in the same direction; the matched
treated-article leftover is \(0.028\ [0.021,0.035]\). The exact vector
reconstruction error is below \(10^{-7}\). Thus the striking noun rewrite is
almost entirely reproduced by substituting the article token.

The top-1 falsification is even more direct (@fig-s1 A). Treated-article replay
recreates the S1-on top noun on 20/20 prompts. Restoring the baseline article
while leaving S1 active restores the baseline top noun on 20/20 prompts.
Phenocopy and rescue residual TVs are only 0.028 and 0.030. The `pilot` example
therefore reads as a causal sequence: S1 changes `a` to `an`; `an` licenses the
`aviator` continuation; returning `a` restores `pilot`.

Across prompts, the vector decomposition confirms that this is not merely a
top-token coincidence: public substitution reproduces nearly all of the total
noun-distribution movement, whereas the matched fixed-token residual is small
(@fig-s1 B).

![The sparse S1 intervention is an extreme public endpoint. A: treated-article replay phenocopies the noun and baseline-article restoration rescues it. B: public token substitution reproduces almost all free-path change. C: around each prompt's article boundary, the free noun distribution jumps while fixed-article paths barely move.](manuscript/figures/fig_mediation_decomposition.png){#fig-s1 width=98%}

The magnitude is created at the latent-to-symbol boundary. On 19 bracketed
prompts, gains separated by at most 0.0039 straddle the article argmax. The
free-path noun distribution moves 0.938 TV and article substitution alone
moves 0.939, with vector cosine 0.9998. Over that same interval, fixed
`a` and fixed `an` distributions each move only 0.014 TV (@fig-s1 C). A
16-fold tighter float32-head search yields the same qualitative result, showing
that coarse bfloat16 logit levels are not the mechanism. Exact two-article
mixtures from \(\tau=0.1\) to 1 replace the greedy discontinuity with graded
public influence, but the policy component remains aligned with the total.

This is a transmission result, not evidence against latent planning. S1 may
reflect future-relevant state at the pre-article position. What the assay rules
out is interpreting its large free-generation noun effect as comparably large
private persistence.

## Target information can remain privately effective

The S1 result could still suggest that this task is fundamentally public:
perhaps once the article is fixed, upstream state has little remaining control
over the noun. We therefore ask the complementary question directly. Holding
article identity fixed, can target-specific state at the pre-article position
still alter the later lexical prediction? It can. A dense residual sensitivity
reference first establishes
reachability: on held-out same-article pairs, a target residual patch changes
the target-minus-source noun logit by \(6.44\ [4.19,10.06]\), versus 0.14
for matched-norm random directions.

More conservative natural-state-derived directions provide the primary private
evidence. At 270M and native strength, fixed-article target-minus-source movement
is \(0.77\ [0.47,1.13]\) logits for 12 between-class pairs and
\(0.96\ [0.67,1.27]\) for 12 within-class pairs. Wrong-target effects are 0.15 and
0.13; sign reversal moves the contrast in the opposite direction. The
greedy article changes on 0/24 pairs, so the observed greedy free-path changes
survive article fixing. Under \(\tau=0.1\), public TV is 0.002 or less while
private TV is 0.043--0.064, depending on condition. At \(\tau=1\), a
graded public component also appears, so these patches are private-dominant at
low temperature rather than exclusively private under every policy.

The target direction shifts the later noun substantially more than the
wrong-target or sign-reversed controls at both scales (@fig-private A), and the
movement arises primarily by enhancing the intended target rather than merely
suppressing the source (@fig-private B). The normalized assay replicates private
target influence at Gemma 3 1B. Effect
sizes do not increase monotonically with scale, and we make no scale-law claim.
Together with target, wrong-target, reverse, and random controls, the result
establishes a second causal endpoint: target-relevant upstream state can affect
the noun while visible article identity is held constant. S1 and the residual
patches need not implement the same mechanism; they demonstrate that both
routes are available in the model-task system.

![Target-specific private causal control. A: with article identity fixed, natural-state-derived target directions shift the target-minus-source noun contrast more than wrong-target and sign-reversed controls at both scales. B: the effect is primarily target enhancement rather than source suppression. Points are semantic families; intervals bootstrap families. These targeted patches establish private-route capacity, not a spontaneous carrier switch.](manuscript/figures/fig_natural_carrier_regimes.png){#fig-private width=94%}
